title: Concept
description: One video idea with a hook of its own and an arc that lands, written before anything is built. A creative-director writes exactly one of these into concepts/<slug>.json; the story-doctor reads it before it is built; the chief-editor reads them all and picks.

lang.description: BCP-47 tag for the ON-SCREEN text and the narration: 'en', 'es-MX', 'pt-BR'. Not the language of this file, whose keys and notes are always English.

subject_quota.description: How much of this concept the main person may occupy. It is declared HERE, per concept, and the reviewer checks the built variants against this number instead of against a fixed one. Ceilings per kind are in skills/reel-forge/references/concepts.md.

kind.description: first_person: the person is the story (POV, talking to camera). recap: the trip or the event told through them. place_first: the place, the food or the animal is the protagonist and they are a guest. custom: anything the user explicitly asked for.

max_ratio.description: Ceiling for cuts_with_subject / cuts in the built variant. Over it, the reviewer blocks.

min_ratio.description: Floor, when the concept stops working without the person (a first-person POV with two cuts of them is a different video).

note.description: Required on 'custom': who asked for it and why.

arc.description: The spine of the video: what it promises, how it grows and how it lands. Cuts without an arc are what makes a finished video feel like it was interrupted: it opens something, never develops it and stops mid-air. Every second in `structure` belongs to one stage of this arc.

hook.description: 0-3 s. If you cannot write it in one sentence, the concept is not ready.

visual.description: What you SEE. The strongest shot in the catalog, not the first one chronologically.

text.description: What you READ, in the output language, written for that language and not translated word for word.

resource.description: The catalog id that opens the video.

ends_s.description: The second the hook is done. Past 3 s it is no longer a hook, it is an intro, and the viewer already left.

promise.description: The debt the hook takes on. A hook that promises nothing has nothing to pay back, and a promise that is never paid is exactly what 'it cuts off' means.

what.description: What you are telling the viewer is going to happen, in one sentence: three proofs, the place at the end, why nobody goes back.

paid_off_at_s.description: The second the viewer gets what they were promised. It sits inside the close, or in the turn just before it, never in the first third.

development.description: The middle: the beats that carry the promise from the hook to the close, in order. Each one adds something the previous one did not. A beat may run long if it carries a `mini_hook`; more than 5 s with nothing new and no reason to stay is where a viewer leaves. A video that needs only one beat is a clip, not a concept.

at_s.description: When this beat lands, on the same clock as `structure`.

raises.description: What this beat adds that the one before it did not: a new fact, a bigger scale, a complication, a change of place. If you cannot write it, the beat is filler and its seconds belong to another one.

mini_hook.description: The reason to stay for the next beat: a question left open, a cut on a sound, a counter going up.

turn.description: The high point or the flip: the moment the video stops being what it looked like. Optional in a gag or a pure photo dump; without it, anything past ~30 s flattens out.

close.description: The planned landing, never whatever was left over. Shipping without one is what the feedback 'it ends too abruptly' is about. The five moulds that work are in references/concepts.md.

kind.description: punchline: the gag pays off on the last cut. back_to_hook: the opening shot returns, now meaning something else. final_fact: the number or the name that reframes everything. question: an honest question that invites an answer. loop: the last frame joins the first so the replay is seamless.

shot.description: The last thing on screen, by catalog id or in words.

text.description: The last caption, in the output language. Optional: a close can land in silence.

lands_because.description: Why this ends the video instead of stopping it: what it answers, closes or flips. 'It is the last clip left' is not a close.

block.description: One cut. Blocks are ordered and do not overlap.

resource.description: A catalog id that EXISTS. Inventing one invalidates the whole concept.

what.description: What is on screen in this cut.

role.description: Which stage of the arc these seconds serve. Cuts with no role are the ones that get trimmed first when the video runs long.

text.description: On-screen copy, written in the output language. Nothing under 0.8 s can be read.

sound.description: Music, diegetic audio, a hit, silence.

effect.description: At most two per cut. No cross-fades, wipes or sparkles.

subject.description: Whether the main person is in this cut. This is what the quota is counted from.

says.description: The narration line that is being spoken over this cut, if any. It is what ties voice to picture: if the voice names something concrete here, this cut has to SHOW it. The reviewer checks that pairing to 0.25 s.

variant.description: One way of executing this same concept. A viewer who watches two variants one after the other has to see a different video, and that means a different MIDDLE: every non-base variant uses at least 40 % material the base does not (`new_resources`), measured again after rendering by compare_variants.py (under 60 % of shots shared). A new hook, close or voice over the same middle is a hook test, not a variant; another song is never one (the clean files carry no music), and neither is the same video shorter.

differs_in.description: What a viewer notices FIRST. `base` is the reference cut (at most one). `hook`: opens on another shot (hook_resource). `close`: lands on another shot (close_resource). `voice`: narrated where the other is not. `shots`: another selection or order of the story. Whatever it says, a non-base variant also carries `new_resources`.

hook_resource.description: Required when differs_in is hook: the catalog id this variant opens on, not the concept's own hook.

close_resource.description: Required when differs_in is close: the catalog id this variant lands on, not the concept's own close.

target_duration_s.description: A variant may run shorter or longer than the concept, but it keeps the whole arc: a short variant cuts development beats, never the close.

new_resources.description: Catalog ids this variant uses that the base does not: at least 40 % of the concept's `resources` count. Other moments of the same story, other Live Photos, the neighbours of a favourite. Required on every non-base variant.

id.description: short-name-with-hyphens; it names the folder and the delivered files.

angle.description: The angle you were assigned. Variety comes from the angles handed out, not from asking for 'something different'.

family.description: Format family, in references/concepts.md. Two concepts of the same family in one delivery is a repeat.

target_duration_s.description: How long THIS story needs, decided by its arc and not by a house length. Guide ranges, to argue against and not to obey: gag or ranking 10-20 s; recap or POV 20-35 s; storytime, guide or documentary 35-75 s. Past 75 s the material has to earn every second. If there is more story than time, this number goes UP; if there is padding, it goes DOWN.

duration_rationale.description: Why this number and not 10 s less or 15 s more, counted in beats: 'hook 3 s + three proofs of 7 s + turn + close = 31 s'. Writing a duration you cannot justify is how every video came out the same length.

bpm.description: Measured on the real preview, never assumed. Required when cut_to is 'beat'.

narration.description: true means every variant that carries voice ships a voice-script.json (schemas/voice-script.schema.json), and its captions are cut from the generated voice, not from estimates.

music.description: The sound, with its source. Never an invented 'trending' song.

resources.description: Every catalog id this concept uses. Must be a subset of the catalog.

variants.description: Two to five ways of executing this same concept, each one a video a viewer can tell apart from the others: another hook, another close, the voice on or off, or mostly different shots (`differs_in`). One may be the `base`.

missing.description: Material the idea wanted and the catalog does not have. Say it here; never request it as if it existed.

then.description: Past 35 s a video without a turn flattens out: the viewer has already understood the pattern and there is nothing left to wait for.
